theory.intro: The longest straight line in a box runs through its inside, from one corner to the opposite corner. Finding it needs Pythagoras twice: the base face diagonal first, kept exact, then the diagonal itself. Round only at the end.
facts: A **space diagonal** joins two opposite corners through the interior of the solid.
Find the base face diagonal first with $\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}$ and keep it exact.
Only round at the very end; squaring a rounded surd loses accuracy.
steps: Find the length of the relevant face diagonal, keeping it exact.
Calculate the length of the space diagonal using Pythagoras’ theorem.

mastery.solution_text:
The space diagonal of a cube with edge $a$ is $\sqrt{a^{2}+a^{2}+a^{2}}=\sqrt{3a^{2}}$.
$\sqrt{3a^{2}}=15$
$3a^{2}=225$
$a^{2}=75$
$a=\sqrt{75}\text{ cm}$
Volume: $a^{3}=75\sqrt{75}\approx649.5\text{ cm}^{3}$
Surface area: $6a^{2}=6\times75=450\text{ cm}^{2}$

Find the longest space diagonal of the box and compare it with $2\text{ m}$.
$AC=\sqrt{1.2^{2}+1.0^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{2.44}\text{ m}$
$AG=\sqrt{(\sqrt{2.44})^{2}+1.4^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{2.44+1.96}$
$=\sqrt{4.4}$
$\approx2.10\text{ m}$
The longest diagonal is about $2.10\text{ m}$, which is greater than $2\text{ m}$, so the pole fits.
